title: Model Attributes and Constraints
description: Use Prisma model attributes like @id, @default, @unique, @db, and @@map to control database behavior.

data.text: Prisma attributes let you configure database-level behavior directly in your schema. Common attributes include `@id`, `@default`, `@unique`, `@db`, `@@map`, and `@relation`.

items: **@id** — Marks the field as the primary key
**@unique** — Enforces uniqueness at the database level
**@db.VarChar(n)** — Maps to a native varchar column
**@updatedAt** — Automatically updates the timestamp on changes
**@@map("table_name")** — Maps the model to a differently named table
**@@unique([...])** — Creates a unique constraint on multiple fields

data.title: Attributes in Practice
data.content: A model using various Prisma attributes.
data.code:
model Post {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug      String   @unique @db.VarChar(200)
  title     String   @db.VarChar(255)
  content   String?
  published Boolean  @default(false)
  authorId  Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("posts")
}
